answer: Each identity runs one receiver that timestamps a coded signal from the mast each epoch and files the delay. An auditor recomputes the delay from the distance to the zenith mast and the public zephyr wind vector, since wind shifts sound speed; an error over 2% or a reused code burns the 80-credit bond. A receiver costs 55 plus an 80 bond; the k-th channel costs 55+9(k-1), so 1,000 fakes pay 4,550,500 plus 80,000 locked. A rented-receiver ring replaying timestamps fails: each delay depends on its own distance and wind path. Honest operators pay 55 once and recover the bond after a clean epoch.
